ember_relay_help: Firewalled Ember users can't be reached directly, so an Ember user with an open connection passes connection requests on to them. Ember handles this automatically.
ember_relay_open_title: When your connection is open, firewalled Ember users can relay through you. Each one counts for 6 hours after they last shared through you.
ember_relay_firewalled_title: You're firewalled, so another Ember user needs to pass connection requests on to you. Ember finds one automatically.

ember_dht_udp_unreachable_hint: Ember is still working out your public address. Your shared files are published as soon as it knows it.
ember_dht_firewalled_publishing_hint: Your router or firewall is blocking direct connections, so other users reach you through a relay. Sharing and downloading still work.

ember_health_relayed_fix_interface: Ember is kept on one network interface, so your router can't forward ports for it. If that's a VPN with port forwarding, forward TCP {tcp} and UDP {udp} there.
ember_health_relayed_fix_forwarded: Ember's ports are already forwarded on your router, yet other users still can't reach you. Your internet provider may share one public address between customers (carrier-grade NAT), or a firewall on this computer may be blocking Ember.

wizard_welcome_desc: Ember finds files on the Ember Network, KAD and eD2K servers, and stays compatible with eMule-family clients (eMule, aMule, eMule Xtreme, and others).
wizard_welcome_hint: Let's configure your preferences. You can change any of these later in Settings.
wizard_feature_dual_desc: Ember Network and KAD work together so files are found even when one network is quiet, and you can add eD2K servers any time.
wizard_feature_epx_desc: Ember peers share source lists with each other for faster downloads. Non-Ember clients are unaffected.
wizard_feature_secure_desc: Protocol obfuscation, IP filtering, and credits-based upload priority.
wizard_nickname_desc: This is how you appear to other peers on the network. You can use the generated name or pick your own.
wizard_nickname_hint: Shown to eMule users, eD2K servers and your friends (channels use a separate username). Up to 128 basic Latin letters; accented letters, other scripts and emoji count as 2 to 4 each.
wizard_folder_desc: Choose where Ember saves downloaded files. Completed files will appear in a "Downloads" subfolder which is automatically shared.
wizard_folder_picker_hint: Ember can only save downloads to a folder chosen here, so this path cannot be typed in.
wizard_ports_desc: Ember needs a TCP port (file transfers) and a UDP port (KAD and the Ember Network, which carries friends, channels and chat). The defaults work for most users. If your VPN forwards only one port number, you can use the same number for both. Turn on UPnP to have your router forward them automatically.
wizard_ports_upnp_hint: On by default: Ember asks your router to forward these ports so other users can connect to you directly. Turn it off if you use a VPN with its own port forwarding, or if you forward the ports yourself.
wizard_ports_hint: If UPnP is off, you may need to manually forward these ports on your router for best performance (HighID).
wizard_bandwidth_desc: Limits keep Ember from filling your connection. When you open this step, Ember measures your connection once and fills in limits of 80% of the measured speed, unless limits are already set. On very fast connections the test uses up to about 1.2 GB. Set a limit to Unlimited if you have bandwidth to spare.
wizard_speed_test_recommended: Limits set to {up} up / {down} down (80% of your measured speed). You can change them.
wizard_speed_test_failed: Speed test failed. You can set limits manually.
wizard_connect_desc: Ember joins these networks automatically when it starts.
wizard_connect_kad_desc: Decentralized peer discovery via the Kademlia DHT. Starts with the app and stays connected; Ember relies on it to find sources.
wizard_connect_ember_desc: Always on. Ember's own network starts with the app and needs no setup.
wizard_connect_hint: eD2K servers are optional: connect to one from the eD2K Servers page, or turn on auto-connect in Settings → Network.
wizard_launch_at_login_label: Start Ember when I sign in
wizard_launch_at_login_hint: Ember starts quietly in the system tray, so the files you share stay available and it reconnects faster. You can change this later in Settings.
wizard_ready_desc: Here's a summary of your configuration. You can change any of these later in Settings.
wizard_ready_restart_note: Ember restarts once to apply these settings.

stats_overhead_source_exchange_help: Peers swapping lists of who else has a file you are downloading, so Ember finds sources without asking a server.
stats_overhead_file_requests_help: Asking peers for the pieces of a download, and answering the same question for peers uploading from you.
stats_overhead_epx_help: Ember Peer Exchange: Ember users passing each other lists of sources for the files they download. Only used between Ember users.
stats_overhead_ember_dht_help: Ember's own overlay: finding Ember peers, announcing your shared files to it, and carrying friend and channel traffic.

friends_undiscoverable_title: Friends cannot find you right now.
friends_undiscoverable_body: Ember couldn't reach the Ember Rendezvous server, so friends who don't already know your address can't find you. Ember keeps retrying on its own. If this doesn't clear, check your internet connection and any firewall or VPN that might block Ember.
friends_chat_locked_body: Its encryption key could not be recovered, so past messages cannot be read and new ones cannot be sent. Nothing has been deleted or replaced. Restore an Ember profile backup, or put back a copy of chat-history.key made on this computer under the same user account, and your history comes back. Everything else works as normal.
friends_firewall_body: Friends can still reach you for chat, browsing and transfers — Ember connects around your router automatically. Port forwarding or UPnP makes connections faster and more reliable.
friends_firewall_body_symmetric: Your router uses a strict (symmetric) NAT, which Ember cannot connect around. Friends who are also behind a firewall won't be able to transfer with you. Enable port forwarding or UPnP in your router to fix this.
friends_how_share: Share your Friend Code, or add theirs with Add Friend.
friends_how_mutual: Chat is available as soon as they are on your list — messages wait if they have not accepted yet. Browse unlocks only when the friendship is mutual.
friends_how_priority: Friends who download from you through Ember get priority upload slots and jump ahead in your queue. This doesn't apply to ordinary eMule connections.
friends_how_encrypted: Chat messages are end-to-end encrypted on the way and stored encrypted on this computer. Your IP address, message sizes and timing may still be visible, and there is no forward secrecy.
friends_requests_verified_explainer: “Verified” only means the sender's identity signature checked out. It says nothing about who they are — accept requests from people you recognise.
friends_request_verified_title: This request was signed by the Ember identity it claims to come from. That doesn't tell you who the person is.
friends_request_unverified_title: Ember couldn't confirm this request came from the identity it claims. Only accept if you know who this is.
friends_empty_sub: Share your Friend Code above, or add someone else's. You can chat (end-to-end encrypted) as soon as they're on your list; once they add you back you can also browse each other's files, and friends get upload priority.
friends_my_status_hint: Friends see this while you are online. When you are offline, they see Offline.
friends_my_status_idle: Shown as Away while you are idle
friends_encrypted_chat_title: Chat bodies are end-to-end encrypted in transit and encrypted locally; connection and timing metadata may remain visible
friends_copy_id_hint: Ember's internal ID for this friend, useful for troubleshooting. It can't be used to find them: share Friend Codes for that.

kad_type_lifecycle_help:
Contact types, as in eMule:
  Active — has answered, known for 2 hours or more (most reliable)
  Established — has answered, known for 1–2 hours
  Recent — has answered, known for less than an hour
  New — has not answered yet, or is being rechecked
  Dead — stopped answering, will be removed
  Bootstrap — a starting contact from nodes.dat or a bootstrap that has not answered yet

wizard_from_emule: Filled in from your eMule settings.
wizard_folder_from_emule: eMule's incoming folder. Ember saves finished downloads in a “Downloads” folder inside it, and unfinished ones in a “Temp” folder.
wizard_ports_from_emule: eMule's ports, so port forwarding set up for eMule keeps working. Don't run eMule at the same time.
emule_import_staged_message: It is applied when Ember restarts. Cancelling puts any moved downloads back where they were.
emule_import_toast_problems: The eMule import finished with problems. See Settings → Backup & import.
settings_general_desc: Appearance, language, identity and window behavior
settings_nickname_hint: Shown to the eMule users and eD2K servers you connect to, and to your friends. Channels show your channel username instead.
settings_nickname_site_tag: Add Ember's website after my nickname for eMule users
settings_nickname_site_tag_hint: eMule users and eD2K servers see you as “{name}”. Friends and other Ember users always see your nickname alone.
doctor_intro: Checks whether other people can reach this computer, says what Ember already does about it, and suggests what to try.
doctor_verdict_reachable_body: Other people can connect to this computer directly.
doctor_verdict_relayed_body: Other people can connect to you over TCP, so eMule users reach you directly. Your UDP port is closed, so some KAD and Ember connections go through a buddy or relay and take a little longer to start.
doctor_verdict_limited_body: eMule users who are firewalled themselves cannot download from you, and you reach fewer sources. Friends and channels still work through Ember's relays.
doctor_verdict_checking_body: Nothing has tested your ports from outside yet: KAD's firewall check and the eD2K server login have not answered so far. Meanwhile, Ember's relays carry what cannot connect directly.
doctor_verdict_untested_body: Ember could not test whether others can reach you: the outside check did not run, and neither KAD nor an eD2K server has tested your port. Friends and channels still work through Ember's relays.
doctor_verdict_offline_body: Ember is not connected to any network right now.
doctor_helping_relay: Relays carry the connections that cannot reach you directly.
doctor_helping_buddy: A KAD buddy passes on requests from people looking for your files.
doctor_helping_punch: Ember can still connect directly to many peers by having both sides connect at once (hole punching).
doctor_fix_port_in_use_body: Often eMule itself, still running. Close it, or choose another port below and restart Ember.
doctor_fix_restart: Restart Ember to use your new connection settings
doctor_fix_restart_body: The ports or UPnP setting you saved take effect when Ember restarts. Until then these checks describe the settings it is running with. Run the check again after the restart.
doctor_fix_windows_firewall_body: Ember can add the two inbound rules it needs. Windows asks for permission once.
doctor_fix_carrier_nat: Your router doesn't have a public internet address
doctor_fix_carrier_nat_body: Your router is behind another router or modem, or your provider shares one address between customers (carrier-grade NAT). If there is a second router or modem-router, forward the ports on it too or set it to bridge mode; otherwise ask your provider for a public IPv4 address, or rely on Ember's relays.
doctor_fix_vpn: You are connected through a VPN
doctor_fix_vpn_body: If your VPN offers port forwarding, forward TCP port {tcp} and UDP port {udp} in its settings.
doctor_fix_bound_interface: Ember is kept on one network interface
doctor_fix_bound_interface_body: Your router can't be asked to open ports for it. If that interface is a VPN with port forwarding, forward TCP port {tcp} and UDP port {udp} in its settings.
doctor_fix_enable_upnp_body: Lets Ember ask your router to open its ports. Takes effect after a restart.
doctor_fix_router_upnp: Your router did not open the ports
doctor_fix_router_upnp_body: Turn on UPnP in your router's settings, then try again.
doctor_fix_forward_ports: Forward the ports on your router
doctor_fix_forward_ports_body: In your router's port forwarding settings, send TCP port {tcp} and UDP port {udp} to {lan}.
doctor_fix_offline_body: Check your internet connection, then check again.
doctor_fix_checking: Check again in a few minutes
doctor_fix_checking_body: The KAD firewall check needs answers from other peers, which can take several minutes after Ember connects.
doctor_fix_untested: Connect to KAD or an eD2K server
doctor_fix_untested_body: Either one tests whether others can reach you, within a few minutes of connecting. Then check again.
doctor_fix_clock_body: Set the date and time to update automatically in your system settings.
doctor_upnp_enabled_toast: UPnP is on. Restart Ember to start using it.
doctor_action_declined: Not done: Windows did not give permission.
doctor_firewall_confirm: Windows will ask for permission to let Ember accept incoming connections: one inbound rule for TCP and one for UDP, for Ember only. Ember's older rules are replaced; nothing else changes.
doctor_detail_tcp_taken: The TCP port is taken by another program
doctor_detail_udp_moved: The UDP port was taken, so Ember moved to another
doctor_detail_stood_down: Not used: the internet doesn't see your router's address, usually because of a VPN
doctor_detail_vpn: Not needed: your connection goes through a VPN, so its port forwarding is what opens ports
doctor_detail_bound_interface: Not used: Ember is kept on one network interface
doctor_detail_not_mapped: The router did not open the ports
doctor_detail_carrier_nat: Not public: behind another router or your provider's shared address
doctor_detail_closed: Closed: nothing answered on the port
doctor_detail_filtered: No answer: blocked on the way
doctor_detail_rate_limited: Not checked: the hourly limit of outside checks is used up
doctor_detail_busy: Not checked: Ember's test server is busy; try again in a minute
doctor_detail_another_program: Something answers, but Ember could not open this port: another program holds it
doctor_detail_logging_in_again: LowID from before your port opened; logging in again for a HighID
doctor_detail_symmetric: Symmetric: hole punching works with fewer peers
doctor_not_probed: Ember's test server could not check your ports from outside this time, so this result comes from the KAD and eD2K checks alone.
doctor_report_ports: TCP port {tcp}, UDP port {udp}; local address {lan}; public address {ip}
doctor_statusbar_title: Find out why other people cannot reach this computer well
doctor_offer: Other people cannot reach this computer well. Check the connection to see why.
error_doctor_failed: Could not read the network state
error_doctor_unknown_action: That fix is not available here
settings_channel_username_hint: 2–12 letters (A–Z) or numbers, no spaces. Shown to people in your channels and unique across Ember. Separate from your Nickname under General.
settings_channel_language_hint: Shown as a flag beside your username in channel member lists, so people can tell which language to write to you in. If you speak two, add a second. Nothing is shared unless you pick one.
settings_launch_at_login_hint: Start Ember automatically when you sign in to your computer.
settings_start_hidden_at_login_hint: When Ember starts at sign-in, keep the window hidden in the system tray. Without a tray icon the window opens as usual.
settings_window_on_launch_hint: Where the window appears when Ember starts. Takes effect the next time you launch the app.
settings_close_behavior_hint: What happens when you click the X in the window's title bar. Minimized to the tray, Ember keeps downloading and sharing, and you can reopen it from its tray icon. Exiting stops all transfers.
settings_minimize_to_tray_label: Hide in the tray when minimized
settings_minimize_to_tray_hint: When you minimize the window, hide it in the system tray instead of the taskbar. Without a tray icon the window minimizes as usual.
settings_close_behavior_ask_desc: Show a dialog with both options
settings_close_behavior_exit_desc: Quit the app fully each time
settings_downloads_desc: Where files go, transfer limits, behavior, preview and history
settings_library_desc: Shared folders, who can browse your files, video upload compression, the file name tag, and how files are scanned
settings_watch_shared_folders_hint: New and changed files in shared folders are added to the Library as they appear. Off, the Library picks up changes when you reload it, at the next start, or when a folder is added. On Linux, a very large folder tree can use up the system's limit on watched folders; if new files stop appearing, turn this off.
settings_hash_low_priority: Hash shared files at low priority
settings_hash_low_priority_hint: Hashing reads every shared file once. At low priority it gives way to whatever else the computer is doing, so a large first scan does not slow it down. Off, hashing finishes sooner on a busy computer.
settings_upload_quota_label: Slow uploads after a daily amount
settings_upload_quota_hint: Once this much has been uploaded since midnight, uploads are held to a lower speed until the next day. For metered connections, and for providers that throttle a line that uploads a lot. Downloads are not affected. Counted in gigabytes of 1,000,000,000 bytes, as providers count.
settings_upload_quota_speed_hint: Applies until midnight. A lower limit already in force (manual, alternative or scheduled) still applies.
settings_upload_quota_reached: Quota reached ({used} GB today): uploads are held to {speed} until midnight.
upload_quota_holding_note: Daily upload quota reached: uploads are held to {speed} until midnight.
error_settings_upload_quota_invalid: The daily upload quota must be between 1 and 1000 GB.
error_settings_upload_quota_speed_invali: The upload speed after the quota must be at least 1 KB/s.
library_coll_keep_folders_desc: Records the folder each file is in, relative to the folder that contains all the selected files. Ember recreates them when the collection is downloaded; eMule lists the files without folders.
library_coll_keep_folders_download: Download into a folder named after the collection
library_coll_keep_folders_download_hint: Download the files into a folder named after the collection, keeping the collection's folders inside it.
settings_category_folders_hint: Each download category can finish in its own folder inside Downloads.
settings_shared_folders_hint: Choose the folders you share, and which files only friends can get, in the Library.
settings_max_downloads_hint: How many files download at the same time. The rest wait in the queue and start as others finish.
settings_max_uploads_hint: How many peers you send to at once. Auto picks a number from your upload speed and opens more while there is spare upload capacity. Speed limits are under Bandwidth.
settings_max_connections_hint: The most connections to other users Ember keeps open at once, shared between downloads and uploads. Higher values let you reach more sources and serve more people, but some home routers struggle with very high numbers.
settings_max_conn_per_five_hint: Limits how quickly Ember opens new connections, so home routers are not overwhelmed. 0 means no limit.
settings_auto_away_label: Show me as Away when idle
settings_auto_away_hint: Friends see you as Away after this long without keyboard or mouse input, while your status is Online.
settings_max_sources_hint: The most peers Ember keeps as sources for one download (eMule's default is 400). More can help rare files; each one costs connections and memory.
settings_max_file_size_hint: Ember won't add downloads bigger than this. The default, 593 GiB, is the most the eD2K protocol can describe; eMule itself handles files only up to 256 GiB.
settings_add_paused_hint: New downloads start paused until manually resumed.
settings_completed_first_hint: Lists finished and failed downloads above the ones still running. The More menu on the Transfers page has the same switch.
settings_auto_remove_hint: Take downloads off the Transfers list as soon as they finish. The downloaded files are kept.
settings_tag_downloads_hint: Each download is saved with the tag when it finishes, as “[Ember-P2P] Linux.zip” instead of “Linux.zip”. Downloads that already finished keep their names.
settings_tag_imports: Add [Ember-P2P] to new files in shared folders
settings_tag_imports_hint: Files that appear in a shared folder from now on are renamed on your disk once Ember has hashed them. Files already shared keep their names, and program, settings and hidden files are never renamed. Leave this off if a shared folder holds files other programs rely on, such as games or apps.
settings_name_tag_intro: The [Ember-P2P] tag puts Ember’s name at the start of a file’s name, like “[Ember-P2P] Linux.zip”, so people who find the file from you can see it was shared with Ember. It changes only the name, never the file itself, and you can add it to or take it off any file in the Library at any time.
settings_delete_permanently_hint: When you delete a file in the Library or use Delete File on a finished download, delete it right away instead of moving it to the Recycle Bin. You are asked to confirm when turning this on.
settings_delete_permanently_hint_trash: When you delete a file in the Library or use Delete File on a finished download, delete it right away instead of moving it to the Trash. You are asked to confirm when turning this on.
settings_preview_player_hint: Leave empty to open previews with whatever your system uses for that file type.
settings_preview_player_pick_failed: Could not choose a media player
settings_preview_priority_all_hint: Fetch the start and end of every file first, so videos and music can be previewed sooner. Downloads may finish a little slower. When off, Ember fetches the rarest parts first.
settings_skip_compress_video: Send video uploads without transfer compression
settings_skip_compress_video_hint: eD2K can compress data while sending it to other users. Video files (AVI, MKV, MP4 and similar) are already compressed, so compressing them again only costs CPU. The video itself is never changed.
settings_download_history_hint: Ember remembers files you have downloaded or cancelled and marks them in search results and in friends' shared files, so you don't download the same thing twice.
settings_history_clear_completed_dialog_: Ember will stop marking files you downloaded before. The files themselves are not deleted. This cannot be undone.
settings_history_clear_cancelled_dialog_: Ember will stop marking files you cancelled before. This cannot be undone.
settings_history_clear_all_dialog_messag: Ember will stop marking files you downloaded or cancelled before. Your downloaded files are not deleted. This cannot be undone.
settings_search_desc: Spam filtering, how long searches run, result names and search history
settings_backup_desc: Save your profile to one encrypted file, restore it, or import from eMule
settings_backup_contents_hint: Your identity and secure-identification keys, upload credits, settings, shared-folder list, known files, friends, joined channels, chat history, transfer list, server and KAD contacts, IP filter, learned spam data, and the preferences kept in Ember's window: language, theme, each channel's notification level, favourite and hidden channels, ignored members, search options and history, and which columns each list shows.
settings_backup_excludes_hint: Not included: the files you share, the data of your part-finished downloads, and layout details such as column widths, panel sizes, sort order and open tabs. Restore this on a new machine and you keep your user hash, credits and friendships.
settings_backup_passphrase_hint: A backup contains your private keys, so it is always encrypted. There is no way to recover a lost passphrase.
settings_backup_passphrase_mismatch: The two passphrases do not match
settings_identity_keyring_fallback: Your identity keys are not protected by this computer's keyring, because it could not be reached, so anyone with a copy of this disk could read them. Unlock or set up a keyring (GNOME Keyring or KWallet, for example) and restart Ember to protect them.
settings_backup_where_hint: Save it to an external drive or cloud storage, not just this computer, so it is still there if this computer isn't.
settings_backup_never: No backup has been made from this computer yet.
backup_reminder_message: Back up your Ember profile. If this computer is lost or replaced, a backup is the only way to keep your identity, upload credits and friends. Save it to an external drive or cloud storage, not just this computer.
settings_backup_export_failed: The backup could not be created
settings_backup_restore_hint: The restore is prepared now and applied when Ember next starts, because the files it replaces are in use while Ember is running.
settings_backup_restore_failed: The backup could not be restored
settings_backup_schema_too_new: This backup was made by a newer version of Ember and can't be restored by this one. Update Ember, then try again.
settings_backup_export_skipped_chat_key: Chat history on this device is locked (its key couldn't be read), so the key was left out of this backup. After restoring this backup, chat history stays locked until you restore chat-history.key from an older backup.
settings_backup_preview_missing: Not in this backup, so this device's copy is kept: {files}
settings_backup_preview_chat_key_set_asi: This backup doesn't include the chat-history key. After the restore, chat history will be locked: you can't read or send messages until you restore chat-history.key from a backup that has it. This device's current key is set aside, not deleted.
settings_backup_restore_warning: Restoring replaces your current profile, including your identity and transfer list, with the one in this backup. Your current files are moved to a pre-restore folder inside Ember's data folder, so you can still undo it by hand. Part-finished downloads the backup does not list are not deleted: their data is set aside in an orphaned-… folder inside the Temp folder of their download folder. Shared folders from the backup that this computer has not approved stay unshared until you re-approve them in the Library. Folders on network shares are not restored: choose shared folders again in the Library, and the download folder in Settings → Transfers.
settings_backup_pending_title: A restore is waiting for the next restart
settings_backup_pending_message: {files} files from the backup made by Ember {version}, prepared {when}. They are applied while Ember starts up. Discarding leaves your current profile untouched.
settings_backup_pending_expires: Restart before {when}: a restore still waiting 30 days after it was prepared is discarded at the next start, and you would have to restore the backup again.
settings_backup_pending_discarded: The pending restore was discarded; nothing will change on the next start
settings_backup_restore_staged_message: {files} files from the backup made by Ember {version} are ready. Ember applies them while starting up. Restart now?
settings_spam_filter_hint: Flag search results that look fake or like spam. Flagged results are hidden while Hide spam is on in Search.
settings_spam_profile_hint: Relaxed flags only clear-cut spam, using just your own marks and file names. Balanced also weighs other users' fake ratings and patterns across the whole search, and suits most people. Aggressive flags more, so some genuine files may be hidden.
settings_spam_db_hint: What the filter has learned from results you marked as spam or not spam, and from files you finished downloading. It stays on this computer.
settings_search_timeout_hint: How long a search, or loading a file's notes, waits for results before it stops (30–600). Search results found by then are kept.
settings_save_search_history_hint: Remember recent search queries and suggest them when you start a new search. Turning this off clears your existing history and stops saving new searches.
settings_highlight_matches_hint: Marks the words you searched for in Search results and in Library file names.
settings_filename_cleanups_label: Text to remove from result names
settings_filename_cleanups_hint_prefix: Removed from file names shown in search results to make them easier to read. Downloads keep the real name. Separate entries with | (for example
settings_bandwidth_desc: Upload and download speed limits, alternative limits, a daily upload quota, a schedule and a speed test
settings_max_upload_speed_hint: Unlimited can fill your connection and slow down your downloads and browsing. A limit of about 80% of your real upload speed avoids that; the speed test below can measure it.
settings_max_download_speed_hint: Usually best left at Unlimited. Set a limit if Ember's downloads slow down everything else on your connection.
settings_download_ratio_cap_note: Limited to {limit} ({ratio}× your upload limit) because your upload limit is below {upload}, as in eMule.
settings_alt_speed_hint: Use these limits instead of your speed limits and the schedule. The tray menu and the speeds in the status bar switch them too.
settings_alt_speed_active_banner: Alternative speed limits are on, in place of the limits below and the schedule
settings_uss_hint: Lowers your upload speed automatically when your connection starts to lag, and raises it again when it recovers, up to your max upload speed. Needs a max upload speed to be set.
settings_speed_test_hint: Measures your connection with Cloudflare's speed test, download first and then upload, in about 20 seconds, and suggests limits of 80% of the measured speeds, leaving headroom for browsing and calls. Ember's own transfers during the test are counted in, but the result is less precise while they run. On very fast connections the test uses up to about 1.2 GB of data. Nothing changes until you apply the suggestion.
settings_network_desc: Ports, connections, networks and eD2K servers
settings_tcp_port_hint: Other peers connect to this port to exchange files with you. Default 4662.
settings_udp_port_hint: Used by KAD, eD2K servers, and the Ember Network. Default 4672. Can be the same as the TCP port if your VPN forwards only one port.
settings_upnp_hint: Asks your router to forward Ember's ports automatically, so other peers can connect to you directly. Turn off if you forward the ports yourself, use a VPN with its own port forwarding, or your router doesn't support UPnP.
settings_bind_interface_hint: Keeps every connection Ember makes on one network interface, such as your VPN's. If it disconnects, Ember stops sending instead of falling back to your ordinary connection.
settings_bind_interface_offline: {name} is not connected right now. While it isn't, Ember stays offline and sends nothing through any other connection.
settings_bind_interface_limits: UPnP is off while Ember is kept on one interface, so others can connect to you directly only if the VPN forwards your ports. Name lookups (DNS) still go through your system's resolver.
settings_upnp_off_for_interface: Not used while Ember is kept on one network interface: your router can't forward ports for traffic that leaves another way.
settings_stun_keepalive_hint: Helps other peers reach you when UPnP can't, for example behind carrier-grade NAT (CGNAT). Ember regularly contacts public STUN servers to keep your router's ports open and tells peers which public ports to use. It pauses itself on networks that change ports for every connection, as many VPNs do, and then uses the ports above.
settings_auto_connect_server_hint: Connects to your last eD2K server when Ember starts. If you have never connected to one, Ember picks a High priority server from your list, or eMule Sunrise. If the server can't be reached, Ember keeps retrying it every few minutes; to use a different one, connect to it on the eD2K Servers page.
settings_update_servers_hint: Ask each eD2K server you connect to for the other servers it knows, and add them to your list.
settings_update_servers_aria: Update server list when connecting to a server
settings_filter_servers_hint: Apply your IP filter (under Security) to eD2K servers too: blocked servers are removed from your list and Ember won't connect to them.
settings_relay_for_peers_hint: Let other Ember users who can't connect to each other directly pass their transfers through you. This is what makes transfers work behind strict routers. It uses part of your upload speed, within your max upload speed, for people you aren't trading with.
settings_networks_hint: Both are always on and connect when Ember starts. The Ember Network carries friends, chat and channels and finds files shared by other Ember users; KAD finds sources on the eMule network and checks that your ports are reachable.
settings_security_desc: Obfuscation, IP filter and anti-leech filter
settings_obfuscation_hint: Disguises your eD2K and KAD traffic so internet providers find it harder to recognise and slow down. Used with every peer and server that supports it, as in eMule. It does not hide your IP address.
settings_ip_filter_hint: Blocks addresses on a list of known bad actors (ipfilter.dat), such as fake servers and anti-P2P monitoring. To download, import or edit the list, use the Security page in the sidebar.
settings_filter_incoming_hint: Also applies the IP filter and private-address blocking to peers that connect to you. Outgoing connections and KAD and eD2K UDP traffic are always filtered. Leave this off if unsure: many VPN addresses are on blocklists, so turning it on can stop VPN users from downloading from you.
settings_block_private_hint: Ignores peers with local-network addresses (such as 192.168.x.x or 10.x.x.x), which can't be reached over the internet. Turn off only to share with computers on your own network.
settings_allow_shared_browse_hint: Lets anyone using eMule, aMule or another eD2K program see the full list of files you share ('View Files'). When off, they are told your list is private. What friends can see is set under Friends.
settings_antileech_hint: Refuses uploads to known leech clients: modified eMule versions that take more than they give back. Peers are recognised by the program name and version they report.
settings_antileech_patterns_prefix: One pattern per line (a regular expression, not case-sensitive), checked against the program name and version each peer reports.
settings_antileech_restore_dialog_messag: Replace your custom anti-leech patterns with the built-in defaults. Unsaved edits and custom patterns will be lost.
settings_antileech_errors_title: These patterns are not valid and are not being used:
settings_antileech_toggle_failed: Couldn't turn the anti-leech filter on or off: {error}
settings_friends_desc: Chat, files from friends and what friends can see
settings_friend_overrides_hint: Friends can see when you're online, chat with you and send you files, as set below. You can also give one friend different settings, which take priority over these — open them with the gear button on their card on the Friends page.
settings_friend_chat_hint: Send and receive messages and files with friends. When off, messages they send are discarded, not saved for later, and their file offers are declined. You can't send messages or files either.
settings_friend_files_hint: Let friends send you files in chat. When off, their files are declined and chat keeps working. Settings you give one friend (gear button on their card) can still allow them.
settings_friend_browse_label: Let friends browse my shared files
settings_friend_browse_hint: Friends can see the list of files you share. When off, you can still browse theirs if they allow it.
settings_friend_browse_folders_label: Show friends which folder each file is in
settings_friend_browse_folders_hint: Friends browsing your files see each one's folder, starting from the shared folder's name. Nothing above the shared folder is shown. Both of you need Ember 1.8.0 or later.
settings_friend_chat_read_receipts_hint: Let friends see when you've read their messages. If this is off, you won't see theirs either.
settings_chat_mailbox_label: Deliver messages while friends are offline
settings_chat_mailbox_hint: Messages to a friend who is offline wait for them on the Rendezvous server for up to a week, end-to-end encrypted, and messages they send you while you are away wait for you. The server cannot read them, and nothing in them identifies you or your friend. Works with friends on Ember 1.7.4 or later. Private messages with channel members you have already written with wait there too, for members on Ember 1.8 or later.
settings_chat_disappear_hint: Applies to new messages with every friend you haven't given a timer of their own (gear button on their card). Messages you send disappear from both computers; a friend on an older version of Ember keeps their copies. Files you receive stay in the Chat Files folder.
settings_max_friends_hint: How many people can be on your friend list. Raise it if you hit the limit when adding someone. Lowering it does not remove anyone already on the list.
settings_chat_attach_auto_label: Download files from friends automatically up to
settings_chat_attach_auto_hint: Larger files wait for you to accept, and so do programs and scripts of any size. Set to 0 to always ask. Received files are saved to the Chat Files folder inside your download folder. Chat Files is not shared.
settings_chat_window_reopen_label: Reopen the chat window at launch
settings_chat_window_reopen_hint: If the chat was in its own window when Ember closed, that window opens again when Ember starts, except when Ember starts in the tray. Kept on this computer.
settings_channel_file_offers: Who can send you files in channels
settings_channel_file_offers_hint: This only controls who can ask. You always choose whether to accept, and nothing is downloaded until you do. Accepted files go to the Channel Files folder, which is not shared.
settings_restart_dialog_title: Restart Ember to apply this change?
settings_restart_dialog_message: You changed your {reason}. This takes effect after Ember restarts. Restart now?
settings_spam_reset_dialog_message: This forgets every file you marked as spam or not spam, the files trusted because you downloaded them, and the file names and source IPs learned from them. The built-in checks keep working, and the filter learns again as you mark results. This cannot be undone.
settings_values_adjusted: Some numbers were outside their allowed range and were changed to the nearest allowed value. Check the fields you just applied.
settings_validation_number_empty: A number box is empty. Enter a number in it before applying.
settings_save_live_apply_deferred: Settings saved, but Ember was too busy to apply some network changes right away. They take effect the next time Ember starts.
settings_restart_failed: Restart failed: {error}. Close and reopen Ember to apply your changes.
settings_spam_reset_failed: Failed to reset spam filter data
error_network_unavailable: Ember's network service didn't answer. Try again in a moment; if this keeps happening, restart Ember.
error_self_add: You can't add yourself as a friend
error_chat_encrypt_failed: Couldn't encrypt this message. Reconnect to this friend and try again.
error_clipboard_text_too_long: That is too much text to copy at once.
error_clipboard_task_failed: The clipboard couldn't be reached. Try again.
error_clipboard_write_failed: The system clipboard couldn't be written. Try again.
error_secure_friend_v2_required: Secure friend connection unavailable. Ask your friend to upgrade Ember, then reconnect.
error_timed_out: Ember didn't get a reply in time. Try again.
error_backup_invalid_destination: Choose a location and file name ending in .emberbackup
error_backup_invalid_source: That backup file could not be opened

settings_share_ember_installer_hint: Helps people who cannot reach GitHub get Ember over eD2K. When Ember updates, it keeps the installer it updated with in the Ember releases folder of your download folder and shares it, and removes the previous one.
settings_seed_ember_releases: Share every file of each new release
settings_seed_ember_releases_hint: For a computer that stays on. kad_stat_stun_keepalive_help: Ember regularly asks a public STUN server which address and ports the internet sees for you. This also keeps your router from closing those ports while nothing is happening. Active means it is running now; it isn't needed when your router forwards Ember's ports.

kad_tiles_kad_note: The external IP, firewall, TCP and UDP readings come from eMule's KAD network, which checks your connection separately from Ember, so they can differ from Ember's reachability above.

channels_page_subtitle: Public and private channels on the Ember Network. Your IP address isn't posted in the channel, but members you connect to directly, for example to send or receive a file, can see it.
channels_limits_note: Channels have no forward secrecy: if a channel's key leaks, past messages captured with it can be read. Bans are enforced by each member's Ember, not by a server, and a banned person can still read a public channel. A channel has one owner; use Transfer ownership to hand it over. Files go to one member at a time, up to 2 GB, and only after they accept. Between two firewalled members they go through a relay and are slower. Public listings can be spammed.

feeds_own_reach_none: Followers can't fetch this feed right now: other peers can't connect to you directly, and Ember's server can't be reached. See the Ember Network page.
feeds_discover_cannot_share_title: Its publisher was online in the last few hours, but its files can't be fetched right now.
feeds_item_other_feed: Downloading for another feed you follow, into its folder
feeds_own_opened: That is one of your own feeds, so it is opened in My feeds.
feeds_state_not_seen: Last found on the Ember Network {when}. Its publisher may have stopped publishing it; the files you have stay, and Ember keeps looking.
feeds_state_not_seen_spoken: Not found on the Ember Network for a while. Its publisher may have stopped publishing it; the files you have stay, and Ember keeps looking.
feeds_deleted_notice: The publisher deleted this feed. What you downloaded stays, but nothing new will come.
feeds_discover_show_hidden_body: Every feed and publisher you hid comes back in Discover.
feeds_quota_title: You can have up to {max} feeds.
feeds_quota_full: You have {max} feeds, the most you can have. Delete one to make another.
feeds_share_after_publish: Your feed's link works once you publish it.
error_feeds_list_too_large: This feed's list is too large to publish. Remove some files, or shorten their notes.
feeds_auto_desc: Downloads each file the publisher adds from now on, as soon as Ember sees the update. Files already in the feed are not downloaded: use Download for those.
feeds_auto_max_item: Largest file in MB (0 for no limit)
feeds_auto_max_day: Most in any 24 hours, in MB (0 for no limit)
feeds_auto_hint: Programs, scripts and other risky file types are never downloaded automatically, and nothing is downloaded automatically when the disk is nearly full.
feeds_publish_public_hint: A published feed is public: anyone with its link can see its title, description and files, and that you publish it.
feeds_pick_one_mine: Pick a feed to edit it, or create one.
feeds_publish_up_to_date_title: Nothing has changed since the last publish. Ember republishes the feed every hour on its own while it runs.
feeds_followers_hint: Followers online in the last few hours, counted {when}. Ember counts again every 30 minutes.
feeds_item_downloads_hint: Followers who finished downloading the file from you. Each counts once; one who got it all from other sources isn't seen.
feeds_not_published: Not published yet. Followers only see changes after you publish.
feeds_delete_confirm_body: It stops being published, and its link stops working for good: a new feed gets a new link. Followers keep what they already have. If it is listed in Discover, it may still show there for a while.
feeds_add_files_none: There are no files to add yet. Only files you share with everyone, once they have finished hashing, can go in a feed.
feeds_disabled_body: Feeds run on the Ember Network. Turn it on to update or publish feeds.
feeds_strip_unsaved: You have unsaved changes. Save keeps them here; publishing also sends them to followers.
feeds_saved_toast: Saved. Nothing is sent to followers until you publish.
feeds_unpublished_changes: Your changes are saved but not published yet. Followers see them once you publish.
feeds_discard_body: Your changes to this feed have not been saved.
feeds_picker_not_shown: Hidden because they are not shared, shared only with friends, or still being checked: {count}
feeds_picker_full: This feed is full: it holds at most 2,000 files.
feeds_picker_over_room: Space left in this feed: {room}. Select fewer files.
feeds_picker_showing_first: Showing the first {shown} of {total}. Filter to narrow it down.
feeds_picker_draft_note: Files you add join the feed's draft. Followers get them once you publish.
feeds_empty_following_body: A feed is a list of files someone keeps up to date. Paste a feed link to follow it, and whatever they add shows up here.
feeds_empty_mine_body: Make a list of files you share with everyone. People who follow it see each file you add.
feeds_no_new: Nothing new since you last looked.
feeds_items_dropped_one: {name} was left out because it is no longer shared with everyone.
feeds_items_dropped_other: {count} files, including {name}, were left out because they are no longer shared with everyone.
feeds_discover_empty_body: Feeds their publishers chose to list show up here, whether or not the publisher is online. A feed that is not listed can still be followed with its link.
feeds_discover_off_body: Discover needs the Ember Network to find public feeds. You can still follow a feed by its link.
feeds_discover_hint: Anyone can list a feed, and Ember does not check what is in it. As with any download, following one shows your address to whoever serves its list.
feeds_discover_active_title: Its publisher was online in the last few hours.
feeds_discover_hide_publisher: Hide all feeds from this publisher
friends_action_feeds_title: Show the feeds they publish in Discover
feeds_visibility_link_hint: Only people who have its link can find it.
feeds_visibility_public_hint: Anyone can find it in Discover, as well as by its link.
feeds_listed_hint_unpublished: It appears in Discover once you publish it.
feeds_listed_off_toast: Taken out of Discover. Others may still see it there for a while.
feeds_listed_confirm_body: Anyone can then find this feed in Discover and see its title, description and files. This takes effect now, without Save or Publish.
feeds_private_note: Files you download from this feed go in its own folder under Feeds in your Ember download folder. They are not shared and do not appear in the Library, unless you turn on Share files from this feed.
feeds_shared_note: Files you download from this feed go in its own folder under Feeds in your Ember download folder. You share them from there, and they appear in the Library.
feeds_share_desc: Shares this feed's files like your other shared files, including ones still downloading, so other followers can get them from you too. Anyone who looks up one of these files sees you as a source, which, for a file found nowhere else, reveals that you follow this feed.
feeds_share_off_saved: This feed's files are private again
feeds_risky_confirm_title: Download files that can run code?
feeds_risky_confirm_body_one: {name} can run code or change settings on your computer. Only download it if you trust this feed's publisher.
feeds_risky_confirm_body_other: {count} of these files can run code or change settings on your computer, including {name}. Only download them if you trust this feed's publisher.
error_feeds_not_found: That feed could not be found.
error_feeds_item_not_on_disk: That file is no longer on disk.
error_feeds_library_loading: The Library is still loading its files. Try again in a moment.
error_feeds_too_many: You already have as many feeds as one identity may have.
error_feeds_too_many_items: A feed can hold at most 2,000 files.
error_feeds_publish_failed: Could not publish the feed. Try again.
error_feeds_publish_unreachable: Could not reach the Ember Network to publish the feed. Try again in a minute.
error_feeds_publish_unconfirmed: The feed was sent, but too few nodes confirmed it in time. Ember sends it again by itself, so there is nothing to retry, and followers may see it already.
error_feeds_failed: Something went wrong with feeds. Try again.
error_feeds_task_error: Something went wrong with feeds. Try again.
error_feeds_bad_link: That is not a feed link.
error_feeds_own: That is one of your own feeds.
chat_emoji_no_room: Can't add that emoji: the message is at its length limit.
chat_attach_cancel_confirm_body: Part of “{file}” has already been transferred. Cancelling stops the transfer.
error_network_kad_no_peers: Unable to connect to the KAD network. Try Bootstrap on the KAD Network page and use the default nodes.dat.
kad_bootstrap_continues_in_background: Bootstrap is still running. You'll see the result when it finishes.
stats_stale_since: Couldn't refresh the statistics. Showing figures from {time}.
settings_restart_unsaved_message: Restarting closes Ember. Changes not applied yet in {sections} would be lost.
settings_restart_apply_failed: Some changes couldn't be applied, so Ember wasn't restarted. Sections with changes still to apply are marked with a dot.
transfers_add_links_none_found: No eD2K file links found in the text.
search_action_show_in_transfers_title: Already downloading. Show it in Transfers
friends_mark_all_read_title: Mark every conversation as read. Disappearing messages stay unread until you open them.
friends_mark_all_read_failed: The conversations could not be marked as read.
friends_mark_all_read_kept: Disappearing messages stay unread until you open them.
settings_notify_feed_update: A followed feed has new files
ipfilter_watch_blocking: The IP filter could not load its list, so Ember is blocking every peer.
network_bind_waiting: Ember is waiting for {name} to connect and sends nothing until it does.
network_bind_lost: {name} disconnected. Ember sends nothing until it is back.
network_bind_changed: {name} is back with a new address ({address}). Restart Ember to use it; until then nothing is sent.
doctor_detail_blocking_all: On, but its list did not load, so every peer is blocked
doctor_fix_ip_filter_body: The IP filter is on, but its list did not load, so Ember blocks every peer until one does. Download the default list here, or import one or turn the filter off on the Security page.
library_unpublished_friends_only: Shared with friends only, so it is not published to the networks
library_unpublished_offline: Waiting for a network: Ember publishes it once KAD, an eD2K server or the Ember Network is connected
library_unpublished_publishing: Being published. Ember publishes shared files a few at a time, so in a large library this can take a while
feeds_auto_types_all: None ticked: files of every type are downloaded, except the risky types below
feeds_auto_types_some: Only files of the ticked types are downloaded automatically
feeds_held_type: Not downloaded automatically: not one of the types chosen
settings_spam_data_spam_hint: Files you marked as spam. Unmark one to take back the mark and what it taught the filter.
settings_spam_data_not_spam_hint: Files you marked as not spam, and files you finished downloading. Search never flags these; forget one to have it judged like any other file. Files in your Library are never flagged, whether or not they are listed here.
settings_spam_data_names_hint: Names learned from the files you marked as spam, shown in the simplified form (lower case, punctuation removed) that results are compared against.
settings_spam_data_ips_hint: Addresses that offered the files you marked as spam. A result one of them offers is more likely to be flagged as spam.
settings_spam_data_unmarked: {name} is no longer marked as spam.
settings_spam_data_load_failed: The spam data could not be loaded.
server_setup_intro: Choose a password for this page. To show the server is yours, enter the setup code emberd wrote in its log. The code is also in the file emberd-setup-code in emberd's data folder.
server_setup_mismatch: The two passwords are not the same.
server_unencrypted_warning: This connection is not encrypted. Anyone on the network between you and the server can read your password and everything on this page. Use it only on a network you trust, or give emberd a certificate in its config file.
server_reconnecting: Lost the connection to emberd. Reconnecting…
server_download_folder_hint: emberd's config file sets where downloads go (download in [folders]), so it cannot be changed here.
server_backup_export_done: Backup ready ({size}, files: {files}). Your browser is saving it as {name}.
server_settings_desc: Signing in to emberd, and what its config file sets
server_settings_password_changed: Password changed. Every other browser was signed out.
server_settings_sign_out_hint: Signs this browser out. Ember keeps running on the server.
server_settings_config_hint: Change these in emberd's config file, then restart emberd.
server_settings_config_none: None. emberd runs on its defaults and environment variables.
server_settings_browse_under: Folders this page may share from
server_settings_browse_under_none: None, so this page cannot share more folders.
server_settings_restart_hint: Ember stops and starts again on the server, and this page reconnects.
server_settings_logs_hint: Its service manager keeps it too: journalctl -u emberd, or docker logs.
server_settings_update_hint: Update emberd the way you installed it: a newer package, Docker image or download. It does not update itself.
error_server_unsupported: emberd cannot do that. It is only in the desktop app.
error_server_login_required: You are signed out. Reload the page to sign in again.
error_server_cross_origin: emberd refused a request that did not come from its own page.
error_server_wrong_setup_code: That is not the setup code. emberd writes it in its log.
error_server_login_wait: Too many wrong tries. Wait a little and try again.
error_server_wrong_step: Something changed on the server. Reload the page and try again.
error_server_password_unusable: That password cannot be used. Try another.
error_server_auth_save_failed: emberd could not save the password. Check that its data folder can be written to.
error_server_bad_request: emberd did not understand that request. Reload the page and try again.
error_server_internal: Something went wrong in emberd. Its log has the details.
error_server_file_unavailable: That file is not on the server anymore.
error_server_upload_too_large: That file is too large to send.
error_server_upload_failed: The file did not arrive. Try again.
error_sharing_folder_set_in_config: emberd's config file shares this folder. Take it out there.
error_sharing_browse_under_unset: emberd's config file names no folders this page may share from. List them under browse_under in [folders].
server_notifications_default: Allow notifications here to hear about finished downloads, messages and the rest while this page is open.
server_notifications_granted: Allowed. This browser shows Ember’s notifications while this page is open.
server_notifications_denied: Blocked in this browser. To have them, allow notifications for this site in the browser’s settings.
server_notifications_unsupported: Browsers show notifications only for pages served over HTTPS or from this computer (localhost), so this page cannot.
error_server_upload_unknown: That file is no longer on the server. Send it again.
error_server_busy: emberd is busy checking other sign-ins. Try again in a moment.
server_notifications_enabled_hint: Shown by any browser that has Ember open and is allowed to show them.
server_notifications_desc: Notifications in this browser, and the pop-ups Ember shows in its page
transfers_failure_reason_download_folder: Another program is using the download folder. Ember tries again by itself.
settings_history_data_load_failed: The download history could not be loaded.
settings_history_data_removed: {name} was removed from the download history. Search no longer marks it.
channels_library_hint: Folders you keep for this channel alone. While your library is open, the channel's members can browse it and download from it. These folders are never shared on eD2K, KAD or Ember.
channels_library_open_label: Open my library to this channel
channels_library_open_note: Open. Members of this channel can browse it and download from it.
channels_library_closed_note: Closed. Nobody in this channel can see it.
channels_library_no_folders: No folders yet. Add one to offer its files to this channel.
channels_library_pick_folder: Choose a folder for this channel's library
channels_library_too_large: Files over 2 GB are left out for now: {count}
channels_library_truncated: Only the first 50,000 items are offered.
channels_library_load_own_failed: Could not load your channel library
channels_library_browse_hint: Files they keep for this channel. A download arrives in Channel Files and shows in this channel's transfers.
channels_library_closed: Their channel library is closed to this channel.
channels_library_missing: That folder is no longer in their library.
channels_library_download_queued: {name} will arrive as a channel transfer
error_room_library_folder_system: Whole drives, system folders and Ember's own folder can't be in a channel library.
error_room_library_folder_shared: That folder is shared or holds downloads, or is inside or around one that is. A channel library is kept apart from sharing.
error_room_library_folder_overlap: That folder is already in this channel's library, or inside or around one that is.
error_room_library_too_many_folders: A channel library holds up to 16 folders.
error_room_library_folder_not_allowed: emberd can only use folders under the ones its config lists in browse_under.
error_room_library_public_room: Channel libraries are only for private channels.
error_room_library_failed: Something went wrong with the channel library.
error_room_library_folder_gone: That is no longer in their library.
error_room_library_no_answer: They didn't answer. They may be offline.
error_room_library_busy: Too many files are already waiting to download.
error_sharing_room_library_folder: That folder is in a channel library, or holds or sits inside one. Channel library folders are never shared.
channels_deleted_by_owner_title: Its owner deleted this channel. It can't be joined; you can remove it from your list.
error_channels_message_not_found: That message no longer exists. It may have been removed.
error_channels_registry_forbidden: The Ember Rendezvous server refused this change. Only the owner of this channel or name can make it.
error_channels_registry_invalid: The Ember Rendezvous server didn't accept that name. Choose a different one.
error_channels_registry_rejected: The Ember Rendezvous server rejected this request. Try again later.
error_channels_member_not_in_channel: That person is no longer a member of this channel.
error_collections_file_too_large: This collection file is too large to open.
chat_disabled_notice_friend: Chat with this friend is turned off in their own settings. Turn it back on with the gear button on their card on the Friends page.
chat_empty_disabled_friend: No messages yet. Chat with this friend is turned off in their own settings.
chat_dock_chat_disabled_friend: Chat with this friend is turned off in their own settings (the gear button on their card).
chat_dock_chat_disabled_all: Chat is turned off in each friend's own settings. Turn it back on with the gear button on a friend's card on the Friends page.
error_network_stopped_port_in_use: Ember's port is already in use by another program. Close that program or change the ports in Settings → Network, then restart Ember.
error_network_stopped_permission: The system refused Ember access to the network. Check your firewall or security software, then restart Ember.
error_network_stopped: Restart Ember to reconnect. If this keeps happening, report it with the log files from the logs folder in Ember's data folder.

web_runtime_bad_status: Ember's server did not answer properly (error {status}). Check that emberd is running, then reload the page.
web_runtime_restart_lost: Ember's server did not start again. Check that emberd is running, then reload this page.
web_runtime_not_web_address: This link is not a web address.
